correctness.rationale: For F′=min(r(t),f(F)) with locally Lipschitz strictly positive nonincreasing cumulative capacity f and arbitrary finite positive-duration rainfall blocks r_j≥0, scalar flows exist globally and strictly preserve initial-state order. For high rate a>b>0, define v_a=min(a,f), v_b=min(b,f), h(x)=∫ du/v_b and R=v_a/v_b∘h^{-1}, which is nonincreasing because v_a/v_b equals a/b, f/b or 1 on successive capacity regimes. The low-rate flow translates y by duration t; high-rate flow Ψ_s has derivative Ψ_s′(w)=R(Ψ_s(w))/R(w)≤1. Hence high-then-low minus low-then-high in transformed terminal state is ∫_0^t [1−R(Ψ_s(w))/R(w)]dw≥0. Positivity on a positive-measure subset is necessary/sufficient for strict advantage. Zero-intensity intervals commute, and equal intensities tie. Adjacent swaps and strict subsequent order preservation give global descending-maximal infiltration and ascending-minimal infiltration, with opposite runoff. Exact witness f=max(1,3−F), high 4 for log(4/3), low 1 for 1/4 gives final 1 vs 15/16. Independently recomputed rational witness and derivative flow argument. Assumes no ponding, moisture recovery or hydraulic-storage extension.
